task.description: Perform WF-02 Step 2c (security gate, HARD GATE) for REQ-373 per docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md and your own role file .claude/agents/security-reviewer.md. This diff touches a tenant-data path (service_catalog entries are tenant-scoped resources, and the new publish/retire routes and PinResolver.Lookup wiring change how tenant-scoped catalog references resolve during instance creation) -- this is IN SCOPE, do not take the out-of-scope PASS shortcut. Read `git diff main...HEAD` yourself (do not trust ELIXIR-DEV's self-report) and the artifacts_in list above. For each of INV-1..INV-8 in security-invariants.md, determine APPLIES or NOT-APPLICABLE and run its 'How to verify' check for every APPLIES invariant. Specifically scrutinize: (1) the two new publish/retire routes are genuinely gated by :AdminServicesManage (re-derive by reading lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex's actual prefix-match logic against the new route paths yourself, not by trusting ELIXIR-DEV's claim it 'automatically covers' them); (2) no tenant-id/user-input string interpolation into raw SQL anywhere in the new migration or new modules; (3) the retire operation's failure mode for NEW resolutions (verify it fails closed, not open -- a security-relevant property, since 'falls through to current version' vs 'fails outright' has different blast-radius implications for an admin retiring a compromised/broken service version) matches what the design specified and what ELIXIR-DEV actually implemented; (4) tenant scoping -- confirm service_catalog/service_catalog_versions reads/writes remain correctly tenant-schema-scoped (prefix-based), no cross-tenant leak introduced by the new archive table or the new Lookup module. FAIL immediately on any applicable invariant failing -- all BLOCKER, no partial credit. Set this handoff's status to COMPLETED with your genuine independent verdict, commit and push before ending your turn.

invariant_assessment.INV-1: APPLIES -- SATISFIED. (a) service_catalog is a deliberately GLOBAL table (no :prefix scoping), a divergence from decision 0003 that was already REVIEWER-signed-off 2026-08-30 (WF02-REQ191-20260830 Step 2d, recorded in lib/letflow/service_catalog/entry.ex's own moduledoc) -- REQ-373 only adds columns/a sibling table to that already-decided-global table, it does not introduce or expand the divergence. Confirmed no @schema_prefix and no opts[:prefix] anywhere in the new code. (b) the new service_catalog_versions table is created in the same migration with no prefix -- correct, it inherits the parent table's own global-ness by construction, not an oversight. (c) no tenant_id column exists on either table at all (owner_tenant_id is a distinct visibility field predating this diff, unrelated to write-scoping) -- so the caller-supplied-tenant_id attribution hazard 0003's addendum guards against does not apply here.

The migration's one raw execute("UPDATE service_catalog SET published_at = created_at WHERE published_at IS NULL") is a fixed literal string with zero interpolation of any kind (tenant, user, or otherwise).
invariant_assessment.INV-8: APPLIES -- SATISFIED. Heuristic grep hits in the changed/touched files are all `case`/`with` clause patterns (e.g. `{:ok, %Pagination.Cursor{} = cursor} ->`), not bare `{:ok, x} = external_call()` matches. publish/3 and retire/1 both use `with`/`case` with every realistic failure branch handled (:not_found, :duplicate_version, %Ecto.Changeset{}, :already_retired) and are wrapped in Repo.transaction/1 with Repo.rollback/1 on error -- no unhandled crash path reachable from admin-supplied (still authenticated, still not raw external-network) input.

specific_scrutiny_findings.1_route_gating: CONFIRMED by independent re-derivation, not by trusting ELIXIR-DEV's comment. The two new routes are declared `authz_post "/:service_id/versions", :AdminServicesManage` and `authz_post "/:service_id/retire", :AdminServicesManage` in lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex -- this is a DIRECT compile-time policy-key declaration (Letflow.Api.AuthorizedRouter's authz_post/3 macro sets `private: %{policy_key: :AdminServicesManage}` on the route itself), enforced by Letflow.Plugs.Authorize reading conn.private[:policy_key] -- it does NOT depend on Authorization.endpoint_policy_key/2's prefix-match clause at request-enforcement time at all (that function is used by a separate consistency check, not by the runtime authorize plug). Re-ran test/letflow/api/authorization_enforcement_test.exs (16/16 passed, real `mix test` run against Postgres, not read-only inspection) which independently walks AdminServices.__authz_routes__/0, builds the full path '/admin/services/:service_id/versions' and '/admin/services/:service_id/retire', and asserts each resolves to the SAME real, present Authorization.endpoint_policy_key/2 clause (`/admin/services" <> _rest` when method in [POST,PATCH,DELETE] -> :AdminServicesManage) -- no new permission atom was invented, both checks agree, and this satisfies the handoff's 'proven by a test' acceptance criterion via a pre-existing generalized enforcement test that automatically covers any new authz_* route in this router.
specific_scrutiny_findings.2_no_sql_interpolation: CONFIRMED. grep -rn "Repo.query" lib/ priv/repo/migrations/ shows zero hits in any file this diff touches; the migration's raw execute/1 call is a fixed string, no fragment interpolation of tenant/user data anywhere in the new migration or new modules.
specific_scrutiny_findings.3_retire_fails_closed: CONFIRMED, matches design AC4 and matches what ELIXIR-DEV actually implemented (not merely its self-report). PinLookup.catalog_lookup/1: %Entry{status: :RETIRED} -> {:error, :not_found} -- identical to the no-row-at-all case, with no fallback branch of any kind (no 'most recent version', no reactivation). ServiceCatalog.retire/1 flips the SAME row to status: :RETIRED (this schema holds exactly one live row per service_id, not a multi-version-active table), so there is no second, older-but-still-ACTIVE row a resolution could silently fall through to -- fail-closed is a structural property of the schema shape, not merely an if-branch choice. Confirmed via source read of both service_catalog.ex's retire/1 and pin_lookup.ex's catalog_lookup/1, cross-checked against the design doc's own AC4 language.
specific_scrutiny_findings.4_tenant_scoping: CONFIRMED, no cross-tenant leak. service_catalog / service_catalog_versions are both deliberately GLOBAL tables (pre-existing, REVIEWER-approved divergence from decision 0003, see INV-1 above) -- there is no tenant schema for a query against them to leak across, by design. PinLookup.build/0's catalog_lookup/1 performs `Repo.get(Entry, service_id)` with no prefix, consistent with that global-table design and with Engine.pin_lookup/2's own prefix parameter being unused (matches the pre-existing 2-arity spec). No new tenant-scoped read/write path was introduced by this diff; the archive table (service_catalog_versions) is equally global and carries no tenant_id or prefix concept, by the same inherited design.
